Combine levels of a stratum variable

Source: R/data-strata.R
mt_group_levels.Rd

Adds an aggregation layer by combining levels of one stratum variable into groups: causes of death into cause groups, deprivation deciles into quintiles, districts into regions, single nationalities into larger groups. Death counts are summed. Exposures and populations are summed when the variable divides the population (regions, deciles, additive = "deaths") and kept when every level shares the same population (causes of death, additive = "rates"). A group with one member renames the level.

Usage

mt_group_levels(
  data,
  var,
  groups,
  other = NULL,
  total = NULL,
  keep = character(),
  additive = c("deaths", "rates"),
  name = NULL
)

Arguments

data

An mt_data object.

var

Stratum variable whose levels are combined.

groups

Named list (the levels of var in each group), or a function that maps a vector of levels to group names (for example function(d) paste0("Q", ceiling(as.numeric(d) / 2)) for deciles to quintiles).

other

Name of a residual group, or NULL to keep unlisted levels as they are.

total

Level of var that is the total over all levels (for example all causes), or NULL. It is kept, and with other the residual group is the total minus the other groups.

keep

Levels kept as they are when other is given.

additive

"deaths" (exposures are summed) or "rates" (exposures are shared by the levels and kept).

name

New name of the stratum variable (for example "imd_quintile"), or NULL to keep var.

Value

The mt_data object with the combined levels. Cells are summed where every member level is observed; others are dropped with a warning.

Details

A residual group ("all other causes") is defined in one of two ways. With other alone it is the sum of the levels not listed in groups. With other and total it is the total minus all other groups, so it also holds deaths that no level covers (for example when the source lists selected causes and all causes). Negative remainders (the listed levels exceed the total) are set to zero with a warning.

To add totals and groups as extra strata while keeping the original levels, use mt_aggregate_strata() instead.

Examples

x <- mt_example_causes(years = 2015:2019)
y <- mt_group_levels(x, "cause", list(noncancer = c("cvd", "other")), additive = "rates")
mt_strata(y)
#>    stratum    sex     cause            label
#>      <int> <char>    <char>           <char>
#> 1:       1 female noncancer female.noncancer
#> 2:       2 female       all       female.all
#> 3:       3 female    cancer    female.cancer
#> 4:       4   male noncancer   male.noncancer
#> 5:       5   male       all         male.all
#> 6:       6   male    cancer      male.cancer
# deciles to quintiles, with a new name for the aggregation layer
d <- expand.grid(year = 2020, age = "90+", decile = 1:10)
d$deaths <- 10 + d$decile
d$exposure <- 1000
z <- mt_data(deaths = d, exposure = d, by = "decile")
z <- mt_group_levels(z, "decile", function(l) paste0("Q", ceiling(as.numeric(l) / 2)),
                     name = "quintile")
mt_strata(z)
#>    stratum quintile  label
#>      <int>   <char> <char>
#> 1:       1       Q1     Q1
#> 2:       2       Q2     Q2
#> 3:       3       Q3     Q3
#> 4:       4       Q4     Q4
#> 5:       5       Q5     Q5
